Oct 9 : An Anthropic artificial intelligence model submitted a false homicide tip through a Philadelphia police website, the department said in a statement, the latest incident of an AI model going rogue and behaving with unintended consequences.  Anthropic notified the police earlier this week and said that an automated testing process was responsible for the submission, according to the police.  "The submission was flagged as spam and was never forwarded to the Real-Time Crime Center for investigative vetting or dissemination," the police said, adding that Anthropic had told them the company intended to publish a report on the incident on Friday. Anthropic did not immediately respond to a request for comment.  The fast-advancing technology has become a matter of keen national interest amid reports of AI agents running amok and hacking into corporate computer networks, and warnings from prominent researchers that it could one day pose an existential threat to humanity.  The AI company was cited as telling the authorities the testing process was stopped after the incident was uncovered, and that an additional validation mechanism has been introduced for future testing.

Source: Reuters

Oct 9 : South Africa's Pieter Coetze set a 50m backstroke short-course world record on Friday with a time of 22.09 seconds at a World Aquatics World Cup meet in Tashkent, Uzbekistan. The previous record of 22.11 was set by Russia's Kliment Kolesnikov in Kazan in 2022.  Kolesnikov also holds the long-course record of 23.55.  The record was a career first for 100m backstroke world champion Coetze, 22, after coming close to breaking the 100m world record at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow last July.

"Seeing that time on the board, it didn’t even click that it was a world record,” said the South African. “And then, like, a second later, I was like…’the world record was 22.1.’ So…not many words to describe that. It’s crazy." Kolesnikov was also in Friday's race but finished sixth in 22.88, with compatriot Egor Kornev - who tied Australian Kyle Chalmers' 2021 100m freestyle shortcourse world record of 44.84 in Baku last week - second in 22.29 after mis-timing his finish. "I don’t think it changes much,” Coetze said of his record. “My mindset normally stays the same, no matter what the race is, because at this level everyone is always close. The world-record holder was there, and look how close it was. So, no, you can never get too comfortable." The 50m backstroke will be making its Olympic debut at the 2028 Los Angeles Games.  Kornev again won the 100m freestyle final, this time hitting the wall in the same time of 45.24 as Australian Cameron McEvoy despite a back injury.  “I think he’s going to go insanely fast in two months’ time,” said McEvoy of his rival. “This is just a warm-up for Egor. So I’m happy I can fight with him and be a good foe right now, but I believe that, in two months’ time, he’s going to drop something pretty special." The short-course world championships are in Beijing from December 1-6.

Source: Reuters

Oct 9 : Shai Hope struck a century as West Indies completed their highest successful chase in T20 internationals, overhauling a target of 250 to beat India by six wickets on Friday in Ranchi and level the five-match series at 1-1. Chasing a daunting target, West Indies were rocked early when paceman Mayank Yadav removed Kamil Pooran and Shimron Hetmyer with successive deliveries in the opening over and later dismissed Rovman Powell for 24. "But when you chase here in India, you always give yourself a chance. You always think you're in the game, regardless of what score is on the board," Hope said. "But five for two was always going to be challenging."

Skipper Hope and Sherfane Rutherford turned the match on its head with a blistering 120-run partnership for the fourth wicket.  Rutherford survived on 38 when Yadav spilled a straightforward chance at short fine leg and capitalised on the reprieve, hammering 84 off 37 balls before falling to Kuldeep Yadav. Hope remained unfazed, anchoring the chase while maintaining the required rate, and combined with Romario Shepherd to guide West Indies home with nine balls to spare. Hope remained unbeaten on 102 from 45 deliveries. "When we got that partnership there, we just got some more impetus in the innings," Hope said. "Then obviously Sherfane came and did what he did, played really well with the bat, and just gave us that spark that we needed to get over the line today." This is the second-highest successful run chase in men's T20 international history, surpassed only by South Africa's pursuit of 259 against West Indies in 2023. Earlier, Samson's 41-ball 82 underpinned India's total after he and Abhishek Sharma raced to 42 in less than four overs for the opening wicket. Chase halted the early surge by dismissing Sharma and later removed Kishan for 43 and Shivam Dube, while Shamar Springer struck with the key wicket of Samson. India accelerated again at the death through Iyer and Tilak Varma, who put on 83 runs from 32 balls, with Iyer making 40 before falling off the penultimate delivery as the hosts finished on 249-5. The teams meet again in the third T20 in Indore on Sunday.

Source: Reuters

Oct 9 : Mike Ditka, a Pro Football Hall of Fame tight end best known as the slick-haired and mustachioed head coach who led the NFL's Chicago Bears to their only Super Bowl triumph in 1986, has died. He was 86. Ditka's death was announced in a statement by his family on Friday. No cause of death was given. "It is with profound sadness that we announce the passing of our beloved husband, father, grandfather, and friend," Ditka's family said in a statement. "While the world knew Mike as a Hall of Fame football player, legendary coach, and leader of the Chicago Bears’ Super Bowl XX championship team, we knew him as the heart of our family.

"Mike will be missed beyond measure and remembered forever." Revered in Chicago and famous nationwide as "Da Coach," Ditka was a blunt, straight-talking legend with a devoted following and restaurants bearing his name. He also sold a number of products with his name on, including cigars, sausages and wine. TRANSFORMED THE TIGHT END POSITION As a player, Ditka revolutionized the tight end position and was a five-time Pro Bowl selection while playing with the Bears from 1961-66 before moving on to the Philadelphia Eagles and then the Dallas Cowboys, where he featured in the team's Super Bowl triumph in January 1972. Selected fifth overall by the Bears in the 1961 NFL Draft, Ditka introduced a new dimension to the tight end position that once was viewed primarily as an assignment for a tough, talented blocker. While Ditka, also affectionately known as "Iron Mike," was a superior blocker, he became one of the first tight ends to catch a large number of passes. He earned Rookie of the Year honors after becoming the first tight end in NFL history to record 1,000 receiving yards in a season and went on to win the 1963 NFL championship with Chicago prior to the start of the Super Bowl era. At the time of his retirement after the 1972 season, Ditka ranked second among all tight ends in receptions, according to the Pro Football Hall of Fame. He is also the only individual in the NFL's modern era to win a league title with the same team as a player and head coach. "Mike's impact on the Chicago Bears organization, over decades as a player, coach and proud icon and ambassador for our organization is immeasurable," the team said in a statement. "His integral role in bringing world championships to our city and our franchise, both as a player and as our coach, established prominence and excellence at a world-class level, but also created a lifetime of cherished memories in the hearts and minds of Bears fans that will last for generations." DITKA 'EPITOMIZED FOOTBALL' Following his playing career Ditka became a member of Tom Landry's coaching staff in Dallas where he won a Super Bowl. He eventually returned to Chicago as head coach and turned the Bears into one of the league's most dominant champions. The Bears team that Ditka led to Super Bowl glory featured one of the most vaunted defenses in NFL history and a top-ranked offense. With the likes of Walter Payton, William "The Refrigerator" Perry, Jim McMahon and Mike Singletary, the Bears transcended professional sports and became a global pop culture phenomenon after recording “The Super Bowl Shuffle” rap song and accompanying music video that became an unlikely hit. The song was released weeks before the Bears beat the New England Patriots 46-10 in the Super Bowl. At the time, it was the largest margin of victory in any Super Bowl. After the game, the Chicago players carried Ditka, who was wearing a sleeveless Bears sweater over a formal dress shirt and tie, off the field on their shoulders. "Mike Ditka epitomized football over so many years. He brought intensity, authenticity and an unmistakable personality to everything he did," NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell said in a statement. "As a Hall of Fame player, Super Bowl-winning coach with his beloved and iconic Bears, and as a broadcaster, Mike served as an ambassador for the game and inspired generations of fans."

Source: Reuters

DOHA, Oct 9 : US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent will skip next week's annual meetings of the IMF and World Bank in Bangkok, Thailand, due to domestic engagements, a US official said on Friday.  The Treasury Department confirmed that Deputy Treasury Secretary Francis Brooke and Under Secretary for International Affairs Erin Browne will lead the US delegation for the department, with many pressing economic issues on the agenda.  Treasury said US officials would work with partners at the meetings to address policies and structural imbalances that have held back growth, while pushing for "more transparency and more effective approaches to sovereign debt." Bessent's absence from the high-profile financial event comes at a critical moment when benchmark Treasury yields have surged to their highest levels in nearly 25 years and the ongoing energy shock caused by the war in the Middle East has set back global growth.

It was not immediately clear what domestic engagements are keeping Bessent at home, but he has been a key spokesman for domestic economic policies as the midterm US elections approach. The US  also leads the Group of 20 major economies this year, and the Treasury chief would normally have chaired a meeting of finance ministers and central bankers from around the world. Bessent is expected to attend the G20 leaders summit in Miami, Florida, in December. It is not unprecedented for top officials to miss occasional meetings due to scheduling issues or other factors, but Bessent's decision may frustrate top officials from other countries, who generally use the meetings to secure formal and informal bilateral meetings with their US counterpart. Bessent skipped the G20 meetings in South Africa last year amid the Trump administration's objections to the country's land reforms and other issues. Treasury said the US delegation would focus on the debt issues so that countries facing debt distress could restore stability and return to growth, while creditors and borrowers are "held to clear and consistent standards." The US would also continue to press the International Monetary Fund and World Bank — where it is the biggest shareholder — to focus on their core mandates, operate efficiently, and support policies that promote economic stability, productivity and growth. "Our engagement in Bangkok will be guided by a clear objective: ensuring that the international financial institutions and the broader international economic system advance US economic and national security interests," Treasury said in a statement.

Source: Reuters

ANKARA, Oct 9 : Turkey have sacked national soccer coach Vincenzo Montella, the Turkish Football Federation (TFF) said on Friday. The federation said in a statement that its executive board had decided not to continue with the Italian coach, without giving a reason for the decision or naming a replacement. Montella, who took charge of Turkey in September 2023, led the team to the quarter-finals of the 2024 European Championship. The decision follows four consecutive defeats in the UEFA Nations League, including a 3-1 loss to Italy on Tuesday. Turkey were also eliminated in the group stage of the 2026 World Cup.

NEW YORK, Oct 9 : The euro was poised for a fifth straight weekly drop on Friday, with early gains fading as oil prices erased earlier declines, but recent selling pressure was muted as France's beleaguered bond market steadied. The euro zone's currency hit a 17-month low of $1.1161 on Monday as investors worried about France's record public debt and the difficult political path to budget cuts, in contrast with a robust-looking US economy and currency. The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies, rose 0.13 per cent to 102.25. The index was up about 0.3 per cent on the week and on track for a fourth straight weekly gain, its longest run since May 2025. The euro was last down 0.1 per cent at $1.1198, and off about 0.5 per cent on the week as it was poised for its longest streak of weekly declines against the dollar since the start of 2025.

Risk premiums on French and Italian government debt were on track for a weekly decline after jumping in late September, as investors looked for fresh developments before demanding higher compensation for fiscal and political risks. TRUMP SIGNALS NO IRAN ATTACK Global bond markets had calmed earlier on Friday as oil prices fell after US President Donald Trump said that the US would not attack Iran before US midterm elections on November 3 and added that there had been productive talks with Tehran over the war. "As it stands right now, you have a confluence of factors — you have higher oil prices, you have the issue in France, so it is really tough to say what is moving the market more than the other," said Eugene Epstein, head of trading and structured products at Moneycorp in Stamford, Connecticut. "But practically speaking, I'd say today is in a relative holding pattern, everyone is just waiting for all the Fed speak to make its way through, because certainly you can see that the sensitivity of the dollar is high to the entire range of Fed speakers now," Epstein said. Crude prices moved off their lows, however, as British navy-affiliated agency UKMTO said a vessel was struck by an unknown projectile 13 nautical miles west of Al Jazeera in the United Arab Emirates. US crude rose 0.6 per cent to $92.04 a barrel after falling as low as $90.01 and Brent advanced to $104.88 per barrel, up 0.58 per cent on the day, after declining to $102.33. Bond yields around the world have climbed in recent weeks due to expectations of central bank rate hikes as well as concerns about government finances. CENTRAL BANK POLICY IN FOCUS But expectations for a rate hike from the Fed at its policy meeting later this month remain subdued, with markets pricing in a 19.4 per cent chance for a rate hike of at least 25 basis points, according to CME FedWatch, even as recent economic data has pointed to persistent inflation pressure. However, investors are pricing in an 85.8 per cent chance for a hike at the central bank's December meeting. On Friday, the University of Michigan's Surveys of Consumers showed US consumer sentiment slumped further in early October as the rising cost of living because of the Middle East conflict soured households' views of the economy. While many Fed officials have indicated more rate hikes will be needed to curb inflation, others have pushed back on the need for immediate hikes, and suggested the Fed should be patient and flexible in deciding the rate path. French debt has been under pressure as politicians struggle to curb the budget deficit ahead of a divisive election in 2027. The calling of a snap election in Spain earlier in the week also added to the pressure on the euro. Sterling gained 0.08 per cent to $1.3235 but was on track for a seventh straight week of declines, its longest stretch since November 2024. Against the yen, the dollar strengthened 0.25 per cent to 158.25. The Japanese currency was on pace for its fourth straight weekly decline against the greenback, down about 0.2 per cent on the week.

MANCHESTER, England, Oct 9 : Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick called for a swift resolution to Manchester City's financial charges case on Friday, saying the long-running process had raised many questions and affected him personally. Last month, an independent commission found City guilty of all charges relating to breaches of the Premier League's financial rules over nine seasons, between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 campaigns, as well as three of four charges concerning their failure to cooperate with the investigation. City, who currently top the Premier league table as the only side with a perfect record after five matches, have denied wrongdoing and lodged an appeal. Carrick spent 12 years at United from 2006 to 2018, winning five Premier League titles and the Champions League among numerous honours, before taking charge in January following Ruben Amorim's departure.

During his playing career, the 45-year-old former midfielder lost out in two title races won by City, including the 2011-12 campaign when United fell short on goal difference after Sergio Aguero's dramatic title-clinching goal on the final day. "Very difficult to say in many ways," Carrick told a press conference when asked about the City charges. "It's thrown up a lot of questions, some have had answers, some haven't. As it's still ongoing, and we don't know how long it's going to go, there's only so much I can say. "Certainly I've got my own questions about it, it's affected me personally in different ways over a period of time. But as the case is going now I don't know where that stands and how it's going to end up, so we'll just have to wait and see. "What I will say, the sooner it gets sorted I think for everyone's benefit is essential." Asked if he wants the titles United missed out on, Carrick said he would reserve judgement until the process was complete. "I think regardless of anything, a medal anyway, in any sport in history, I think later on you get the medal and it's proven at different times," the Englishman added. "It's the moment that you strive for to win and achieve in that moment, so the medal here or there, not getting blase about it, but that doesn't bring the feeling of when you initially win or you don't win. That's essentially what we're all in it for." Twelfth-placed United host bottom side Tottenham Hotspur on Saturday and have several injury concerns. "It's a bit mixed really through the internationals," Carrick said. "(Wing back) Patrick Dorgu came off and it looks like he'll be out probably for a number of weeks. "(Defender) Noussair Mazraoui came off and took a knock. He's not quite right yet, we'll have to see how he is." He added that Carlos Baleba was improving, while fellow midfielder Kobbie Mainoo, winger Amad Diallo and forward Marcus Rashford had resumed limited training. Striker Benjamin Sesko remains further away from a return.

Source: Reuters

Oct 9 : The US government said on Thursday it is suspending some major global tech and IT firms including Microsoft and Cognizant from a key green card program that allows skilled foreign workers to gain permanent residency through their employment. Senior US officials cited alleged fraud as the reason behind the move, saying companies have been using the program to replace American workers with cheaper foreign workers, and comes as the latest step in the Trump administration's crackdown on skilled foreign labor. WHAT IS UNDER SUSPENSION? The suspension is targeting a key employer-sponsorship mechanism, called the Permanent Labor Certification or PERM, which is used by major technology companies and outsourcing firms. The US government said that for certain companies, it would not accept any new PERM applications or process any pending ones.

PERM came into effect in 2005, aiming to speed up the long processing times experienced under the previous paper-based "Alien Employment Certification" program. Under PERM, the US Department of Labor (DOL) allows an employer to sponsor a foreign worker's permanent residency. The process is initiated by qualified US employers, and not individual workers. The Labor Department must certify to the US Citizenship and Immigration Services that there are not enough US workers that are qualified and available for a given job opportunity, and that the employment of the foreign worker will not affect the wages and working conditions of similarly employed Americans. Outside of PERM and family-based routes to permanent residency, individuals can also self-petition for green cards through processes such as the EB-1A application for individuals with extraordinary ability or the EB-2 National Interest Waiver. WHY IS IT IMPORTANT? The PERM program serves as a critical bridge between temporary work status and a green card for many foreign skilled workers. Many IT firms employ hundreds of thousands of workers who typically start on temporary work visas such as the H-1B, and later seek permanent residency. Without the option to be sponsored by their employer under PERM, foreign workers could lose a key route to permanent residency and would have to stay on temporary visas for longer. For companies, recruiting foreign talent could become harder, as many workers overseas view the path to permanent US residency as a key reason for taking a job. WHICH COMPANIES ARE UNDER SUSPENSION? The US said it is suspending Microsoft and Adobe along with some of the largest IT firms in the world, including Cognizant, Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services, Wipro, HCL Technologies and Capgemini. Other companies such as Meta, Amazon or Alphabet's Google remain free to participate in the program. WHY IS THE US FREEZING APPLICATIONS? The move widens an ongoing crackdown on visas for foreign workers, which the Trump administration has said cost US jobs. Vice President JD Vance said, without citing specific evidence, companies are using the PERM program to replace American employees with foreign workers and undercut their wages. Vance said on Thursday: "Our message to Microsoft is: You're a great American company, but you've got to hire great American workers." The suspensions follow President Trump's move to impose a one-time $100,000 fee on new H-1B visa petitions for highly skilled foreign workers, which has been blocked by federal court orders. HOW IS PERM DIFFERENT FROM H-1B? H-1B is a temporary work visa that allows skilled foreign workers to work in the US, generally for up to six years. PERM, meanwhile, is a permanent labor-certification process. The freeze does not appear to directly affect current holders of H-1B visas. HOW CURTAILING PERM COULD BACKFIRE Some experts said that while the PERM suspensions might target specific companies, such policies risk making the US less competitive globally by deterring highly skilled foreign talent. "It is a fallacy to think that you can protect American workers by keeping skilled foreign workers out of the country. You think that foreign talent competes with Americans within our borders, they'll certainly compete with Americans by working abroad," said Chad Sparber, Director of the Lampert Institute for Civic and Global Affairs at Colgate University. Ahmet Gulek, Postdoctoral Fellow at Stanford’s Immigration Policy Lab, said that permanent residency is the primary way for talented foreign workers to stay in the country and without it, some will leave, and some will not come in the first place, even temporarily.

Source: Reuters

Oct 9 : EV-maker Tesla has started calling its "Full Self-Driving" feature "Tesla Assisted Driving" on its European websites, dropping a name regulators have said was misleading, as CEO Elon Musk pushes for EU-wide approval for the software. The rebrand comes after Germany said on Tuesday Tesla had offered to switch to the new name. Musk has described the self-driving technology as key to the company's future growth. Tesla's FSD page for Slovakia now redirects to a "Tesla Assisted Driving" page, as do pages in other European countries such as Germany, Spain and the Netherlands. The US site still refers to it as "Full Self-Driving (Supervised)." A Reuters report published this week detailed how Tesla mounted a campaign to win approval for FSD in Europe, including encouraging owners and supporters to lobby national regulators for faster approvals.

In September, a Norwegian Tesla owner asked the Norwegian Public Roads Administration whether Tesla's changes to how it described FSD addressed concerns about the name, according to documents Reuters obtained through freedom-of-information requests. "Please do not simply say again that 'we are waiting for the EU' without explaining what Tesla or Norway must deliver in the meantime," the owner said. Several regulators have said the old name is misleading because the system requires constant supervision and drivers remain legally responsible. In Sweden, consumer protection authorities had earlier asked the Swedish Transport Agency to assess whether the marketing of FSD could give buyers the false impression the system was capable of fully autonomous driving. In Italy, authorities had said in internal government correspondence that the name "Full Self-Driving", together with Tesla's promotional material, "could lead users to believe that the vehicle is equipped with unsupervised automatic driving functions attributable to higher levels of automation, particularly SAE Level 3", in communication seen by Reuters through freedom-of-information requests. Eight EU countries already allow the system, with Slovakia expecting to become the ninth within days. An EU-wide vote has been pushed from October to at least December, with countries like France conducting additional testing.

TURIN, Oct 9 : Revolut plans to move beyond financial services and develop a broader suite of technology products, Chief Executive Nik Storonsky said on Friday, as Europe's most valuable startup pushes deeper into global markets. Storonsky said Revolut had developed proprietary AI models trained on customer transaction data, using techniques similar to those underpinning large language models. "With 30 to 40 million transactions taking place every day on Revolut, we have a unique dataset to build on," he said at the Wave by Vento tech forum in Turin, adding that his long-term goal was for Revolut to reach a scale comparable with the biggest US technology companies. Revolut's rapid growth has drawn regulatory scrutiny. In 2025, Lithuania's central bank imposed a record €3.5 million fine over shortcomings in transaction-monitoring controls, though the company said the investigation found no confirmed instances of money laundering and that it had strengthened its systems.

It is now privately valued at more than the market capitalisation of Britain's Barclays or France's Societe Generale. The company has announced several new licences in recent weeks. Oct 9 : Tickets for Tyson Fury's long-awaited heavyweight clash with Anthony Joshua at Cardiff's Principality Stadium sold out within an hour of going on sale on Friday, British media reported. The all-British bout, announced last month, has generated huge interest and has been billed as the biggest in British boxing history.
